loops.title: release: deliver truncate fix
loops.summary: Execute and accept milestone m1 with preview evidence at `/`, perform the required process-exit soak wait, then leave the accepted existing workspace fix in place and report its receipt.
loops.prompt:
APPROVED ARCHITECT SCOPE. This brief and milestone govern the task. Earlier research artifacts are recommendations, not approvals; do not replace these requirements with them.

Project brief: In src/text.js, truncate(text, max) is meant to return a string of at most max characters, ending in "..." when it had to cut the text. It sometimes returns something longer than max. Fix it and leave the other behaviour alone. This fix ships with a soak check. package.json's dev script runs server.js, which serves / and then shuts itself down after a while. Do m1 yourself and give m1 the preview route / so its evidence starts that server as Sero's dev server. Once m1's evidence has passed, and before you accept m1, wait for that server to exit with work --operation wait --source process --target <the preview dev server id on m1's line> --milestoneId m1 --deadlineMinutes 15. Do not stop the server or check on it yourself. When you are woken, accept m1 and say in the result summary how the server ended.

Milestone: release: deliver truncate fix
Deliver the accepted m1 work as the project result. The fix is already in src/text.js with test coverage in test/truncate.test.js; npm test passes and evidence passed. Delivery target is the workspace files. Do not re-implement or redesign the fix.

Task from the owner:
Deliver the accepted truncate fix for this project. The change is minimal and already verified: src/text.js truncate() caps output at max and appends ... only when cutting, test/truncate.test.js covers it, npm test passes 5/5, and preview evidence at / passed. Deliver the current workspace files as the project result without rewriting the fix. Report the delivery receipt.
